text: Write a program that verifies its own assumption instead of trusting it, converting a silent wrong answer into a loud failure. Fill in the two blanks.
answer: sorted[i] <= sorted[i + 1]|new IllegalStateException("not sorted at " + i)
explanation: Verified: it prints `not sorted at 0`. The check costs a linear pass and buys a message naming the exact index where the assumption failed, instead of a wrong search result three call frames later. Chapter 28 makes this the general rule — fail fast, at the earliest point the assumption can be checked, with the caller who supplied the bad value still on the stack.
